correctness.rationale: Poisson regeneration gives an exponential time since reset. Two-state transition equations yield q_i(a), and Laplace transforms give the exact Cauchy covariance. Classical Cauchy determinant identity proves ordered total positivity, exact rank, and full minors. Bernoulli normalization bounds rho strictly by one-half and the gamma=1/n equal-species family attains the limiting supremum. A decreasing scaled log derivative proves unique interior maximum when either local-loss rate is positive, and the exact cubic identifies it. The deterministic-recovery boundary follows from common Bernoulli indicators. Independent exact stationary four-state generator agrees in 1080 comparisons; exact Cauchy minors agree 3801 times; this is corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact latent covariance rank distinguishes one-dimensional common environmental confounding from low-rank factor intuition; the concrete Cauchy structure yields an interpretable determinant and recovery-rate equivalence classes. The sharp 1/2 Pearson cap is a falsifiable numerical boundary of a natural stochastic-null model used in ecological co-occurrence inference; the unique interior hazard peak controls where spurious association is strongest, and the deterministic-delay example precisely bounds ecological extrapolation. These are substantive structural and modeling statements, not merely reassertions of already-known positive confounding.
